KS-2025-SB74.aiSummary: For tax years 2025 through 2027, Kansas residents could get a tax credit for part of the cost of buying lockable gun and ammunition storage. The credit would equal 25% of the expense, up to $250 per taxpayer each year, and any extra over the tax due would be refunded.

KS-2025-SB236.aiSummary: The bill would let adults who were abused or neglected as children get records tied to confirmed reports or investigations of that abuse or neglect. It would affect those adult survivors and the agencies that keep these records. The bill also says the records must not include the name of the person who made the report.

KS-2025-SB132.policyArea: Children and Families, Department for, Children and Minors, Health and Environment, Department of
KS-2025-SB132.aiSummary: Would change child care rules by lowering some license fees and training requirements for day care facilities, child care homes, and child care centers. It would also let day care license holders ask for a temporary waiver of some state rules and let the health and environment secretary run pilot programs to grow child care supply. The bill would move some child care programs to the Kansas office of early childhood and split licensing duties between that office and the health and environment department.

KS-2025-HB2285.aiSummary: The bill would change the state definition of lead-based paint under Kansas’s lead poisoning prevention law for homes. It would count paint with lead at or above 0.009% by weight, or the lower level set by federal law, and would apply to people and businesses covered by that law.

KS-2025-HB2131.aiSummary: The bill would require prosecutors in criminal cases to tell the defense when they plan to use testimony from a jailhouse witness, and to share key details about that witness’s past, deals, and any benefits tied to the testimony. It would also require each prosecutor’s office to keep a record of these cases and send that information to the Kansas Bureau of Investigation for a statewide database. If a jailhouse witness got a benefit for testifying, the prosecutor would also have to notify the victim tied to the case.
